history.text: Hi! What would you like to build? For example, a RAG system over your company's documents, or a chatbot for your team. “Not sure” is always a fine answer along the way.

response.message:
We're building a cited, permission-aware Q&A assistant on Azure over a small synthetic collection, using bounded keyword retrieval and all five of your acceptance criteria. I've drawn it end to end with the services in the diagram: Entra ID sign-in, the Static Web Apps front end, a RAG API on Azure Functions, a Cosmos DB catalog for ACLs, revisions and the keyword index, Blob Storage plus an ingestion function, Azure OpenAI and Application Insights for audit.

I haven't verified any region, quota, model access or account, and nothing is deployed. Our typed generators only cover Azure private storage, so every component except Blob Storage still needs engineering. That's why I left the Azure implementations unset rather than squeeze this down to storage.

The first local test would load synthetic documents with explicit ACLs and use a scripted model in place of Azure OpenAI. It would check that denied chunks never appear in the prompt, citations match current revisions, unsupported questions abstain, edits and deletions change retrieval, and revoking access mid-answer suppresses the answer. A scripted model only shows that this control flow is correct. It doesn't measure real model quality, grounding or abstention, which needs a separate test against a real Azure OpenAI deployment once access is approved.

Which country must the documents and model processing stay in? That decides the Azure region and which models we can use.

proposal.title: Azure permission-aware RAG qualification architecture
proposal.body: End-to-end Azure sketch: Entra ID sign-in, Static Web Apps front end, RAG API on Azure Functions (keyword retrieval, ACL filter, revision recheck, abstention and citations as application modules), Cosmos DB catalog, Blob Storage source documents with an ingestion function, Azure OpenAI and Application Insights. Assumptions: the region is not selected, the model deployment and access are unverified, and only Blob Storage has a typed generator. Everything else needs engineering. Nothing is deployed.

data.label: Signed-in user (browser)
data.description: Existing person using a browser; an external client reference, not provisioned.

data.label: Web app
data.description: Authenticated chat UI; signs in with Entra ID (auth code + PKCE), calls the RAG API with an access token and displays cited answers or abstentions.

data.label: Identity
data.description: Issues tokens for users; the API validates the JWT and maps subject/groups to catalog ACLs. Tenant and app registration are not yet decided.

data.label: RAG API
data.description: HTTP-triggered, token-validated function. Modules: bounded keyword retrieval, ACL filtering before the prompt is built, prompt with citations, abstention when no support, revision and ACL recheck before returning (suppresses on revocation). Returns the answer to the web app. Uses a managed identity for Cosmos DB and Azure OpenAI.

data.label: Catalog, ACLs and keyword index
data.description: Stores document chunks, keyword terms, explicit ACLs, current revision IDs and tombstones for deletions. The API only reads; ingestion writes conditionally.

data.label: Model runtime
data.description: Chat model deployment called by the RAG API with permitted excerpts only. The model, region and quota are unverified. The local test uses a scripted mock instead.

data.label: Content operator
data.description: Existing operator who uploads, updates and deletes synthetic documents and their ACL metadata.

data.label: Source documents
data.description: Private container with versioning; holds synthetic UTF-8 documents plus ACL metadata.

data.label: Ingestion
data.description: Blob-triggered (Event Grid) function: chunks text, extracts keywords, writes ACLs and revisions, and tombstones deleted documents in the catalog. Must be idempotent.

data.label: Audit and telemetry
data.description: Logs queries, retrieval decisions, denials, abstentions and suppressions, without document content.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Leaking denied content through generated answers would breach source permissions.
requirementDrafts.basis: User: "Denied documents never reach the model"; "keep all source permissions".
requirementDrafts.statement: Documents a user is not permitted to read are filtered out before prompt construction and never reach the model.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Stale citations undermine trust and auditability.
requirementDrafts.basis: User: "Known questions cite current source revisions".
requirementDrafts.statement: Answers to known questions cite the current revision of each source used.
When no permitted source supports the question, the assistant abstains instead of answering.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Deleted or superseded content must not be retrievable.
requirementDrafts.statement: Updates and deletions of source documents change retrieval results once ingestion has completed.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Closes the gap between the retrieval check and the response.
requirementDrafts.basis: User: "Revocation during generation suppresses the answer".
requirementDrafts.statement: If a user's access to a cited source is revoked during generation, the answer is suppressed by an authorization recheck before it is returned.

request.message:
Act as a patient architecture consultant and teacher. Start with the exact evidence state. If blocked before checks, explicitly say runtime tests have not run and the design is not yet validated. An empty failures list NEVER means a sound, complete or correct design. Celebrate only named checks that actually passed. Explain the most important remaining issue in plain language and help the user make progress. Do not just recite a checklist or demand that a junior developer repair product internals. Offer a concrete supported correction when possible; otherwise ask one focused question and explain why its answer matters. Help improve this architecture from its current emulation results. Diagnose the first actionable finding. Propose a minimal supported architecture correction only when requirements already justify it; otherwise ask one precise question.
Preserve all required components, existing systems, IDs, established service choices, access boundaries and requirements. Never clear unfinished-work gates, remove workload scope, weaken tests or invent successful validation. A graph proposal cannot repair generator/runtime source or an emulator defect: identify that as product engineering work with a reproducer. Model output is not test evidence. A local emulation pass is not a cloud plan or deployment. After an applied correction, rerun emulation on the new artifact; do not reuse this result.
